long_biography.plain_text:
Lujo Hotel Bodrum marked Koçkar's shift into direct ownership of accommodation. The resort began welcoming guests under Serkoç in 2018, positioning its all-inclusive model around individualized service, food and arts programming. The project applied his knowledge of international visitor flows to a physical destination business.

Koçkar previously established his executive career inside the travel organization created by his older brother, Neşet. As group chief executive, he coordinated holiday distribution across multiple source markets and contributed to major decisions at partner carrier Azur Air, whose supervisory board he chaired. This combination placed him between customer acquisition and transport capacity before the separate Serkoç investment added hotel development to his responsibilities.

uncertainties: The immutable Serhat Kockar target is resolved to Serhat Koçkar. The cedilla is the standard Turkish spelling, while U.S. government records use Koçkar and UK and Swiss registers use Kockar; the Anex role, Antalya geography and Lujo investment align across both forms.

Mandatory Forbes-first searches found no dedicated Serhat Koçkar profile. A Forbes Turkey article directly supports the Anex role and brother-founder distinction but is recorded as an article source rather than a verified personal profile.

Sources differ on Anex ownership: Forbes Turkey called Neşet the sole owner in 2019, the U.S. aviation record described Koçkar-family ownership in 2021, and Interfax called Serhat a co-owner in 2015. The dossier therefore does not assign a current Anex percentage to Serhat and uses his consistently documented chief-executive role.

Self-made — advantaged start reflects Serhat's separately documented Lujo investment and the substantial market access gained through his brother-founded family tourism group. No reliable source documents inheritance of Lujo or Serkoç, and no claim is made that Serhat founded Anex.

Operator is used because multiple strong sources identify him as Anex chief executive and Azur supervisory-board chairman. Lujo makes him an investor as well, but the long operating role remains his clearest relationship to the wealth-producing tourism platform.
A 2024 Swiss commercial-register entry and an Anex-linked UK record place him in Antalya, supporting Turkey as main residence. Exact street details are excluded.

Nationality records conflict outside the immutable Turkish and Maltese values: U.S. and Swiss sources say Turkish, while an old UK appointment lists British. No nationality correction is proposed, and sensitive citizenship analysis is excluded from the biographies.

No reliable birth day, month, year, birthplace or middle name was found. No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia page or personal website was verified; only Lujo's official company website is proposed.

Current and historical vessel ownership, specifications, operations and cohort context are excluded from both biographies. Politics, controversy, allegations, legal matters, private-family detail and volatile tourism figures are also excluded.
